messages:
Anya: Heads up — saw a p99 tail spike during last night's 03:12 UTC burst on the dedicated pool. Notable: p95 steady, p99 jumped ~2.8x.

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler event @ 03:12:17 — scaled 3 -> 8 nodes. reason=burst_detected; prewarm_attempts=0 (backoff).

Kevin: grabbing logs now. I see a cluster of requests that hit fallback kernels and long KV misses. Posting profiler snippet.

Sam: quick profiler dump:
```
kernel_choice_summary:
  fastpath_hits: 86%
  fallback_kernel_hits: 14%  # fallback adds ~80-150ms per token on p99
kv_cache:
  cold_miss_rate_before: 2%
  cold_miss_rate_during_scale: 22%
average_seq_len: 42
most_affected_seq_bins: [48-96]
```

Anya: Thanks. Two hypotheses: (1) batching heuristic grows microbatch size during queue spikes -> larger serialized work when a KV miss forces a slow path, amplifying tail; (2) new nodes come up without KV warmup and the prewarm window/backoff means a bunch of requests hit cold KV + fallback kernel.

Kevin: Confirmed. The microbatcher target is 8 but allows burst growth up to 24 if queue depth spikes. Combined with our kernel selector breakpoint at 64 tokens we get a mismatch for seqs ~48-96, pushing some requests into fallback.

Sam: Proposed quick experiment config to mitigate tail:
```
autoscale:
  prewarm_window: 90s  # current=30s
batching:
  max_microbatch_cold: 8   # current=24
  aggressive_shrink_on_kv_miss: true
kernel_prober:
  prefer_low_latency_on_cold: true
```

deploy-bot: rolling patch queued to runtime-canary with above flags (svc=runtime-canary). canary size=10% of burst traffic.

Anya: Plan: run 4h canary, capture p95/p99, heatmap + tail traces. Acceptance: p99 reduction >=30% without >5% p95 regress. If good, roll to prod. Assigning @Kevin to dashboards and trace capture, @Sam to kernel prober tuning. :thumbsup:

Kevin: I'll add a tail-heatmap and annotate kernel_fallback events. Also going to shift kernel-selector threshold from 64->80 experimentally to reduce fallback at common seqs.

Sam: If canary looks good, we should follow with an autoscale prewarm tuning: backoff reset after successful prewarm, and add a lightweight KV probe during node join to seed hot prefixes.

Anya: Sounds good. I'll open a short RFC and a follow-up runbook for rollback if we see throughput regress. Thanks all.

Kevin: quick note — we should instrument microbatch-size distribution in the telemetry so we can correlate microbatch size vs p99 per-minute. I'll add that metric.

Anya: Great — keep updates in this thread.
